rules.rule: This repository's test conventions: use testify for assertions; table-driven cases where the shape fits; tests must be deterministic and -race-clean (`make test` runs -race -failfast) — flag any dependence on time, ordering, randomness, or network availability; tests that need a real model file must skip cleanly via t.Skip when TEST_MODEL_PATH is unset, never fail; fail fast on setup errors instead of letting them corrupt later assertions; assert observable state, not implementation details. A bug fix must ship its regression test in the same PR — flag a fix with no accompanying test. A boundary/security fix must add a crafted-input regression test (e.g. a GGUF declaring an absurd length or count) — flag a security fix without one.

Memory/TPS estimators that must track their backend's real allocation behavior: file_estimate__llamacpp.go mirrors llama.cpp, file_estimate__stablediffusioncpp.go mirrors stable-diffusion.cpp. Flag: estimation changes without a cited upstream reference or test coverage; per-device RAM/VRAM projections that ignore the offload-layer, context-size, flash-attention, mmap, adapter, or RPC/tensor-split options from file_estimate_option.go; UMA (Apple) and non-UMA cases conflated; input/transformer/output layer accounting drift (the output layer counts within n_gpu_layers, as llama.cpp does). Estimates should stay within roughly 100MiB of actual usage. Layer ownership: estimation math belongs here, not in the CLI or util/.

Shared generic helper packages (anyx, bytex, funcx, httpx, json, osx, ptr, signalx, slicex, stringx). Flag: GGUF-, estimation-, or CLI-domain logic landing here — these packages must stay domain-agnostic; a helper growing beyond a single clear purpose; new exported API without doc comments.

CLI presentation layer (urfave/cli/v2, dot-imports the root library). Flag: parsing or estimation logic added here instead of the root package; changes to flags, defaults, or output tables that drift from the usage examples in README.md and cmd/gguf-parser/README.md — docs and CLI change together; user-supplied values (paths, URLs, device metrics) used without validation.

GGUF parsing core (file*.go, ggml.go, scalar.go, cache.go, ollama_*.go, filename.go). Every input byte is untrusted — boundary checking is the top review priority: any length, count, or offset declared by the file is attacker-controlled, so it must be validated against the remaining file size before allocating, seeking, or slicing (see the ReadString/ReadArray fixes bounding declared lengths by remaining bytes). A crafted GGUF must produce an error — never a panic, an OOM-scale allocation, or an out-of-bounds read; flag any new trust in untrusted file data, and any panic used for control flow. mmap and chunked/ring-buffer reads must not introduce shared mutable state that races. Remote readers fetch through ranged HTTP backed by cache.go — flag full-file downloads and missing context propagation. Registry readers (Ollama/HuggingFace/ModelScope) fail with explicit errors, never partial state. Exported APIs carry doc comments describing behavior, expectations, and constraints; multi-word file names are snake_case.

Two Go modules live here: the root library and cmd/gguf-parser. Flag: a dependency change applied to one module that the other also needs; a new dependency without justification; drift from `make deps` (both modules tidy).

GitHub Actions workflows. code-review.yml is a caller of the org reusable workflow gpustack/.github — flag drift in its triggers, comment gating, concurrency group, with: inputs, or secret names from that reference configuration. ci.yml path-ignore filters must keep skipping Markdown-only changes. Workflow display names stay capitalized (CI, CMD, Sync, Prune, Code Review).

Markdown documentation. README.md usage examples and option tables must stay in sync with the CLI flags in cmd/gguf-parser/main.go — flag a drift in either direction; its Notes section records behavior-affecting version changes. CLAUDE.md must stay in sync with the repo's real structure, Makefile targets, .golangci.yaml, and gen.go — flag stale commands or conventions. AGENTS.md must remain exactly `@CLAUDE.md`. State a fact once and link to it; flag duplicated facts across pages.
